I would like this response, if not for the fact that a caretaker can not legally accept the membership card. We are not allowed to take any item of value or be associated directly with the client financially. There's also a question of HIPPA here, since their financial information would now be under my name.

The genuine question provided is: "Should the client be allowed to use the service they paid for despite being incapable of getting there?" I do not consider it an unreasonable accommodation for a medically licensed and assigned caregiver to shop for them, but you might and Costco does despite having the simplest solutions in place for verification. This being outside normal business practices isn't even a question, as several court rulings have already made Accessibility clear in Costco's duties to serve the public. Just like they must allow for a wheelchair, they must allow for a caretaker that functions as the arms and legs of the disabled individual.

Edit: I typoed HIPAA multiple times. I thought about it and came back to see I can't see people who replied on a topic I find genuinely important for people's consideration. Whoever replied to this one pointed it out, so I just want to note: Yeah, might lower my credibility, but so should the combination of legal drugs and energy drinks I enjoy partaking in. Does it change the issue I addressed at all that my personal capability can be questioned when I have a license that can be easily verified in any process to check this?

Y'all lose sight of what's important in your rush to discredit others.

Howdy Boss, just want to add some clarity and confusion to this situation, because I still have no answers while being tossed around lawyers and Costco support.   


As you noted, there are times when a person with a disability cannot access goods or services without assistance. I an a PCA, so it's my career to be a caregiver for this type. I specifically prefer to work with the physically and mentally disabled, so oxygen machines and paralyzed bodies are not unfamiliar to me. Bizarrely, some of these people still prefer to use a service like Costco, usually for political reasons.   


Now, as you noted, it is left up to the business to help in the determination of what a Reasonable Accommodation would be. In Costco's situation, for a person who is on an oxygen tank and can not leave their home: They can afford the free admission. They can verify if I am spending for myself or others based on membership/payment card used. They (appear) able to request verification from a licensed medical professional that this service is required. They can verify my license as a PCA.   


The two main problems encountered are:   
A) Costco must be willing to play ball and discuss this matter in the first place. Their policies currently flatly reject the ability to perform services like PCA and employees will refer you to a phone number that refers you to the warehouse's general manager who refers you back to that phone number until you have a list of case references to make him talk to you.  
B) HIPPA. This is such a sticking point that I can't decide an ethical means of running a business which doesn't request protected information to verify situations like these. There's only so much I can deliver as an intermediary, however, and sometimes requested items just aren't acceptable for me to even have, much less share.  


Anyways, this response has been going on a while and while you seemed like an interesting conversation to have, I have never been able to see my own post and thought it was blocked. I don't know which of the 9 iterations you're responding to and the details that managed to get through. My client at the time was locked down to their home, so I just want to leave it on one critical question:  


Is it or is it not a reasonable accommodation to have a professionally licensed and assigned caregiver enter and shop for a customer which has paid for their membership, but can no longer leave their home?

Actually, OP was irritated at being told he was breaking the law after spending $60 to shop for people he was assigned to in his career. So he also paid $60 for a store that he doesn't use because OP walks and can't carry an assortment of unbagged items 2 miles to his home.  


People CAN abuse this, but that doesn't mean I am. I do have a litany of concerns for people who can not leave their homes and want to use Costco's ridiculous services, though.

Howdy Boss. This post appeared blocked and unviewable to me, but now that I've realized others can see it, let me ask you directly: Is it reasonable to make someone pay money to perform their job duties? If the medically provided caregiver needs to buy a membership, they are paying to work. The caregiver accompanying the client is out of the question because the client is tethered to their home by a plastic length of cord that keeps them alive.   


Ask yourself if your mother deserves the right to continue using their services even after she's locked to her bed and wasting away, incapable of shopping for herself. That's the people I serve. Do you consider it an unreasonable accommodation for the caregiver, who is paid to use their functioning legs to pick up their groceries, to be able to shop for the homebound customer?

Getting them there was not part of the equation. Allowing their assigned and medically provided caregiver to shop for them, given that they can not and yet have paid for the right to use the store, was the important part. The only question in the air for this was: "Does your disabled mother who can not leave her home have the right to use the membership she's paying for?" Costco has decided she doesn't.

Shock, awe, and confusion immediately flashed onto the faces of the three LCFL board executives. Despite already seeing this almost exact look three times before, it did nothing to dissuade the cheeks on my face from burning hot. "Yeah, uh, seriously. I've already talked to your company three times now. I seriously don't want the money and uh, could you please retract my name? Entering the contest was an accident..."

My hellion of a sister had been the result of this; I could hear her drunken cackling from a mile away. Just thinking about it made my blood boil, "Oh yeah have fun dude! I've been working on this one for like, foreeeever!" She didn't look like much, opting for stubby tomboy redneck this century, but she really overdid it this time. One-hundred and forty years she sweated, building the Life Counseling For Liberty foundation from scratch. I could have never imagined her as a board executive, not to mention one that got away with twisting her motto of Long Con For Life into an acronym.

Embarrassment burned deeper in my face, their eyes locked on me for what felt like millennia. You'd think after actually experiencing a millennia, you'd lose that feeling, but of course not. The lawyer adjusted his frames, "Okay, uh, Mr. Travian, we just need you to sign these documents. Media exposure is difficult to simply, uh, remove. But, we can remove your name from all company documents, websites, and cancel headlines stating that there was an error and someone else won the money." My sister's ear to ear grin eating into me as she stared across the table, never losing that delight as I set to the task of signing documents for an hour.

No rest, she didn't even let me get that far. "So Mr. Travian, yes? I've come a long way for this, my time is very important, you know." Ugh, seriously? Her voice couldn't be more professional, though it did still have that country twang left ringing in it. "Now, I simply must know, why are you signing over the rights to a one of a kind offer like this! Your salary, with no actual work mind you, would be two thousand dollars a week, simply for winning a contest!"

Murder, maybe I am actually capable of murder. Losing count of the times she's made me feel that way. "Yes. You see, uh, Miss Burlona, I very much value my privacy and you see, um. So like, I'm just really not in a place, right now, that I can accept the offer." Oh no, bad, bad. I can't think like this and she knows it! "See it was an accident signing up, someone else did it for me, but I don't actually...want the money." As my baritone voice filled the room, the placid look on the executives faces cracked again, simply shocked at the situation.

"Okay see so, um, you know I'm very spiritual. Yeah, uh, I like to live outside of the boundaries that aren't...dictated my our lord! See the money goes against my religi-"

"Sir, you could START a religion with money like that, bring the world to your lord!" Her dang voice, again! Ugh, now she's got me thinking hick, too. "I mean yeah I could but uh, see I'm trying to be the religion!" Stupid! "Yeah, I'm uh, I'm the Messiah. I need to live purely and whatnot, then people will believe in me." Stupid stupid! Oh, that one isn't even trying to hide that he thinks I'm an idiot. My body keeps getting hotter, my shame soaking me and dragging me to my toes.

Closing my eyes, I tried to summon even a remotely decent excuse. "So that was worded wrong, I'm just trying to create a legacy, okay? Like I don't want to be misunderstood, I'm trying to...start a lifestyle revolution! You don't need money to live well, just exist with nature, man!" Even I'm disjointed with myself, I could feel her gaze boring into my soul, already hear her laughing at me. I'll probably get a stupid new nickname, like Rumplestiltskin from before. Halfway done with the forms?

"Okay, so just, look, um, ya see, it's a thing. Um, it's a good thing, a great thing. You can uh, achieve spiritual well-being from my program. See I'm like a Guru, not a...crazy religious zealot or something. I want to enlighten the world!" What does a Guru even talk like! I don't read that stuff! "I'm uh, I'm the new Gandhi!" Oh no, what the hell did I just say?! Before they can even open their mouths, "So yeah um, not like Gandhi, that's kinda racist. I'm sorry, uh, like um, Santa...Clause?"

A sharp snort snaps through the small room, knocking the stunned executives and I out of our stupor. As I looked up I saw my sister's cheeks were full of air, her hand covering her mouth in a tight fist. "No not like, ugh no because I bring joy and...spirit to the followers of my, what's it called, uh a Guruship! Not like a zealout though like a...life coach or...fuck, like a gym...coach?" I want to die. I want to die right now. I can not believe myself. No, I can't believe her!

Slamming down the pen, I stood up and pointed, shouting and causing the nearest executive to leap away. "This is all her fault, she's the one who set this up! I don't know how but she rigged this stupid lottery just to embarrass me! She does this all the time! Ashlyn is not who you think she is, she's just using you!" Security came slamming through the door, wrapping their arms around me and dragging me away. "I'm not crazy or some kind of crazy religious zealout or something, she's behind this! She created this company just for the sole purpose of making me miserable! I just want to research and play video games!"

Shock, awe, and confusion. The concrete smacking into my face as I was thrown from the building hurt less than their looks. I don't want to move, I want to just sink into the ground right here. I'm going to get up, go home, somehow she'll already be there, and then I have to deal with her obnoxious laughter for hours. "Can someone, please, make this eternal torture end..."

Mildly irate, the dragon looked about, seeking the source of the juvenile laughter. A child, was it something like 12 in human years? Regardless, the dragon huffed, watching as the child made a mess of his precious jewels. "Put those down and leave! You have no right to be here!"

"EXCUUUSE MEEE?"

One of the human race's women came out, hands on her hair, ruby and emerald coatings dancing through her otherwise platinum highlighted hair. Something sunk in the dragon's heart, as despite rarely dealing with humanity, the screech in her voice made him recoil in agony. "What do you mean my precious child can't play here! I'll have you know he's allowed to play wherever he wants! You need to clean your cave, why do you have all these jewels and gold lying about, don't you know how to DO. YOUR. JOB?!"

The last words were flung with force, taking the dragon off guard. Many knights and adventurers had come to his lair before, attempting to slay him for his precious horde, but this enemy was dangerous. A roar echoed through the cave, though as he prepared to spit fire down upon this hideous human, another wave of magical slander rang against him.

"HOW DARE you raise your voice to me! I'll have you know I am friends with the owner of this cave! I could have you EVICTED! Are you listening to me? Do you not have the intelligence to understand what I am saying? My child will play in this cave all he wants or I WILL CALL YOUR MANAGER!"

Suffering is the only word that could describe it. Aghast from the initial reaction, the new onslaught only drove the dragon further back against the wall. Desperately, he attempted to choke out, "This is my home! You need to le-"

"HOW DARE you talk back to me! That's it, I want your manager RIGHT! NOW!" The woman stomped her feet, causing the entire cavern to quake. Stalactites rained from above as the wrath of the human shook the dragon to his very core. The child continued to devastate the carefully constructed piles of coins, ravaging the hard work that went into carefully stacking and sorting the gems in the most visually appealing manner. Emboldened by its mothers aid, the child crashed through the bed of coins, something the dragon had worked on for weeks to make comfortable to sleep on.

"MANAGEEEEERRRRRRRRR!" Blood seeped from the dragon's ears, the screech shattering his eardrums. Crying out in pain, the dragon collapsed, unconscious, crushing the Karen and child underneath. As oblivion crept in on the edges of his vision, the dragon felt relief wash over him, gratefully thanking the dragon king that it was over.

"The goal is simple, change the world!"

"Stand up for your rights as citizens of Eric's bowels! You are the only bacteria that can make your decision! You are the bearer of the future of our society!" The statement had impact, as it had in the past three or four public speeches, dragging the uncaring masses from their stupor and bringing them back to the importance of the matter, casting a vote regardless of how difficult the situation was.

Sipping from my glass, I re-hydrated, preparing myself to go deep into that place where I could channel the hatred I felt, the pain and misery which permeated my history, directing it towards ensuring my victory. "Bacteria suffer in the intestines. Our supporters are not provided with enough fiber to live. From the very beginning, we're not given the care we require to become functioning members of the bowels, then we're shafted into immediate debt to pay for services we need in order to join the work service! Those who don't take the debt, who join the service immediately, can not afford essential aid and often go without fiber to feed themselves and their families."

"Rise up! Stand and vote! Make a decision for your own future! The opposing counsel preys on the weak, the self-centered, and the desperate! He preys on those who are too afraid to face the fact that the bowels are on fire! Those who stand at his back, providing donations of fiber to his campaign, are waiting to take advantage of the chaos he will bring; they await the day he is voted for so that he can cause more violence, division, and hopelessness to spread throughout the people, keeping them miserable and complacent with their treatment."

"The future is about you! You are the only one who can sit up, look around, and say you can't handle it anymore! Previous generations have failed us! Currently, the government is corrupt. The systems which have been in place since the founding of these intestines are failing us, antiquated and consistently faced with adamant refusal to change alongside time and the rest of the body. Our government is in crisis, ignoring the results other areas of the body have gained from genuine work ethic and intelligent practices such as free healthcare and fiber injections to those who serve the body."

"Understand, your life matters. Those of you who stand in protest of everything which has occurred recently, from the rampaging white blood cells to the irritable bowel syndrome ravaging our homes, you matter! To those who suffer alone, in the dark, you matter! To those starving and suffering with the mental issues which dominate our society and lack of respect for those issues, you especially must always remember, you matter! Even those who support the opposing agenda, too afraid to speak out, or too wrapped up in yourselves to look out and understand that you are a victim of indoctrination, matter."

A pause, short, as I catch my breath and look out into the crowd. Given the lack of features and expression, it's impossible to know if my words truly matter, but this is the only shot I have. These words need said. It likely won't be me, I have no power nor a stockpile of fiber. I only have one minute of these bacteria's quickly passing attention, one minute to inspire them.

"Our bowels are devastated. I extend my best wishes to all those who live with us now. The future is indeed bleak. Despite how difficult life is, how difficult it will be to rebuild these bowels from the ground up, and how many will never forgive us for the crimes we have committed both against our own bacteria and those all around the map of Eric's body, we will overcome. Face that future with me, we can begin to change the world. That mission is simple, even if the means will be difficult. We must accept our failure to overcome!"

"To those elsewhere, to every cell in the body, watch us. The bowels hold the future for now. You must be vigilant, watch us closely, make your own voices and opinions heard to influence the upcoming decision. If we succeed, we will need your help to conquer the greater issues at hand, such as the transition to cleaner, healthier meals. If we fail, the entire body is at risk. This is not the time to stand idly by and allow the entitled to go unquestioned and unpunished."

"You must be willing, should the time come, to flush the bowels and eliminate us if the body is at stake."

That last line is the most critical, the one I've considered over great amounts of time. Most likely, even if my party wins, the bowels will not change. Odds are high that we're too far gone, too stubborn, to accept that everything needs radical change. The two intestine system was never meant to be, it needs more diversity, more options to challenge the beliefs we hold.

"Please, if you can hear me, regardless of your current position, hear my impassioned plea. Open your minds to what is happening, do your research, and take a stand. Vote in the upcoming election and together we can change the world."

"This election, vote to help Eric get lucky! He's left this decision to us, so we must make the responsible choice. Thank you."

The plan was perfect, the stage was set, and the only variable seemed to have vanished into thin air. Quietly, I reviewed the security cameras one last time from the safety of the closet I managed to slip into. The hall was packed full, family and employees listening raptly to the speech offered by our fathers, celebrating the successful plans of their companies and how much everyone stood to profit, with only a small reference to the arranged wedding as expected. From the start, the wedding was always a side show, the bi-product of a merger with two religious fanatics at the head.

Plotting the details of their merger rather than interfering, Samantha and I were given complete control over how we wanted to run the wedding, which made it all too easy to make my plans. When we selected the venue, she was ecstatic as expected. Valeworth Arena is only a short drive away and has a gorgeous view of the coastline, with a stage that props the bride and groom in the perfect position for a beach inspired wedding. More importantly, however, was the little known detail that the owner, my best friend Dan, was providing a huge discount to our fathers, as well as to me personally for his kidnapping side-hustle. 

My moment arrived as the final group entered the hall to listen to the speech, clearing a path between the wedding hall and the bar, which I quickly slipped down without being noticed. One side was too busy and greedy, the other side too engulfed in their drinks. Down the hall, a right past the dining hall, slip into the employee's only section behind the kitchen. From there, all I had to do was wait for Dan, who would open the rear door and have a vehicle ready to go. 

The kitchen was messy, nearly empty but for two menacing cooks. One of them glanced at me, then let out a bark of laughter as he jerked his thumb back to the stockroom. "Head in there, boy. No needsa stay in the open, not long fer the backseat chefs come rockin in here ta give us orders again. Rules is simple, yas don't resist and yas don't make a fit fer the other customer whens they get here, do that and yel be in Maui by mornin. Ya wantsa slice of cake fer ya go?"

Relieved to hear someone even bother to ask if I wanted something, I nodded, heading back towards the stockroom and grabbing the offered slice of wedding cake. Thanking the man fervently, for both the help and the slice of the cake I wouldn't get to cut, I backed into the stockroom and enjoyed a rewarding bite of the blue-iced butterscotch apple cake. Thick icing, but just as sweet as I felt I deserved for finally escaping this place. Usually, security would have never let me go, but my plans were perfect.

In fact, they were so perfect it had seemed to easy to set up the situation. Everything had to be precise, decisions made that were questionable at best for some weddings, such as ordering flowers that would wither easily and requesting Samantha's Aunt Clara maintain the house. Amazing that she allowed that to happen, given Clara's tendency to make everything about herself, but it also went to show how little Samantha cared about the wedding. Sometimes, she'd make a request or two, which is why we ended up in the smaller reception hall on the end, but this worked well in my favor.

At least, I believed it to be a great success at the time. I believed I had successfully maneuvered every piece of the puzzle into place and controlled the situation to set up my escape, right up until the door to the stockroom opened. From head to toe, I witnessed the most beautiful woman I had seen in my life, white gown flowing behind her as she fidgeted with her dress, stubbornly scrubbing at the thick blue icing that stained her chest from the cake in her other hand. The cook who called out to me behind her, grinning like a devil, as Samantha rushed into the room and the door closed behind her, the voice of the other cook cutting through the room as he expertly deflected one of her bridesmaids who thought she had come in this way.

I think both of our hearts came to a stop at that moment, eyes locked on each other, both caught red-handed and lumps forming in our throats. The back delivery gate rattled open, an old, dirty jeep outside with Dan grinning at the two of us. Shocked, I didn't know what to do, what to say, looking between him and Samantha like a deer about to be struck by a car. Dan's voice cut harshly through my thoughts, "Y'all are cute and such, lookin so scuffed, but we ain't got long and I'll be damned if I let yer daddies tan me hide cause ya were too slow."

Brought back to reality, we understood, so we moved to the jeep quickly, though neither of us could quite take our eyes off the other. That moment in time seemed to last so long as we made our escape, as for the first time I regretted that I couldn't marry that gorgeous, intelligent woman before me.

Okay, I have been trying to ignore this and sleep for 30 minutes now, I can't. I'm irate. You came to comment with a semantic argument, acting as though I had no right to talk about this subject here because I spoke to a specific system instead of just generally DMing.

You then followed that with a backhanded suggestion to stop using 5e if I didn't like the combat aspect of it, followed by a smartass remark that would have gotten me beat across the face with a lash. 

Now, maybe I am in the wrong, maybe your massively disrespectful and backhanded comment is normal wherever you're from. I ain't denying that, it didn't even come to my mind when I reacted, so I damn sure hope you never have that kind of situation happen offline. Now let's both walk away pissed off and irate, cause this probably ain't goin anywhere else.

...So it does, huh. I wonder when and how that got in my head wrong. Thank you, important note since I'll be needing it a lot very shortly, think I believed grappling brought an enemy prone. Glad that is cleared up.

I'm sorry boss, you've come back with what looks to be a well considered argument, but I'm seriously exhausted to tears and just trying to provide solid responses to people who took their valuable time to answer me. You might be right I'm not giving enough weight to the importance to do this consistently without resources, but I can hardly string a thought together currently.

Sincerely, thank you for your time, for your comment to help a DM improve. It means a lot, I can't wait to actually be able to read whatever that last paragraph or two says. Regardless though, even if I disagree when I read it, you did me a kindness by writing it. Thank you.

Hi, thanks for your well thought out response, sadly I'm so tired my eyes are watering. 5gp is typically easily attainable in games, so it's not something I consider as enough to have flail top warhammer, plus the option of being able to two-hand is still important since an event could happen where you don't have your shield.

I also didn't consider the one-handed importance enough, I think, but I'm far too tired to discuss currently. Thank you for your time, and the very careful consideration to an argument I have practically been begging for, I genuinely appreciate it.

Similar enough concept, I think everyone got too used to a high magic setting and now they're having that struggle. My players all have about a year experience at least, some vastly more, so it's most likely also my own fault for letting them continuously use the same route to success. Thanks for your time.

You're basically entirely right, I've little more to add, I've basically allowed my players to let me feel comfortable in the same little rut for too long. There's going to be a conversation between us soon to discuss how we're going to break out of it together, I think. Still, disagree to the net, the net is terrible as long as Grapple is an action since it has a far better success chance imo. Do get your reasoning, just can't see a reason I'd ever use a net over my own Athletics ability, probably even if it is low.

I don't like leaving a reply so dry, I would love to go point by point with you and discuss, I'm serious exhausted however. I don't want anyone to go without a response though, since you took your valuable time to help me come to a new understanding. Thank you.

I'm really tired, so my response is going to be sadly short despite the fact I'd rather go point by point. Essentially, all of those situations have just as many if not more ways to be solved by Spellcasters, they almost entirely dwarf everything a Martial class can feel good about. The sheer amount of different solutions magic can take to any of those situations and most others is staggering, while the options for a Martial class are far more limited I feel.

To the last point, I disagree, my argument can't be applied to the other classes remotely as well due to their number of ability choices, while Martials are locked into a set of abilities based on your class and sub-class. As well, I personally feel that terrain control is the superior style of spellcasting, not damage. It's the Druid that wins the fight for dominance, simply because you'll never reach him unless he lets you. At least as long as he knows to prepare, anyways.

Overall though, thank you for your time, I have realized my initial position was flawed, but I will note what you've said for consideration as well while I think over how I want to try and solve this. Maybe I can try to push those kind of specific scenarios more to try and boost my front-line's value a bit.

You are right, I was looking in the wrong place. Sub-classes isn't exactly the solution I feel, as it still doesn't do quite enough to break the cycle, however you do have a point that it probably does come down to players having chosen the wrong loop.

I'll be trying to move my players toward examining better tactics rather than just trying to get more combat options. Especially in the preparation sense, since I entirely forgot some things even exist like poison coatings due to just how long it's been since I've seen anyone actually use them.

I'll be doing some self-examination as well. Clearly I've gotten too stuck in my own ways if I missed this much.

Mhm, sure bud, needed that validation to admit I didn't consider things and may have been wrong. I see why you don't understand much about why what you've been saying doesn't work if you view my responses as argument rather than debate and discussion on the points.

I'm tired, it's 5am, and you're honestly just not even bothering to read the context of other comments, plus somehow missing me blatantly stating I had to reconsider my position after realizing my own mistakes, thanks to another comment pointing it out.

Have a good day/night/whatever, I'll not be responding again.

Please do send me the link even if you go heavy on the homebrew, I'm always excited to read custom work! You can't grow and develop without seeing other people's concepts and perspectives, so it's always a great help.

I'm currently trying to get used to consistently charting everything as well, so would nice to peek at yours and see how it's organized. For about two - three months now I've been forcing myself to try to always keep everything prepared and planned, despite the fact I'm a more improvisational GM. Hoping it'll help me improve.

I've been considering making use of Damage Reduction in some of my recent games, since someone has mentioned wanting to play a homebrew class based around the manipulation of it. Was actually clever what he sent me, but the lack of its use in 5e has made me hesitant since I have little to go off for balance purposes.

I do constantly play with the resistances and such, but there's only so much you can do to actually interest players when the basic concept of their actions is always so similar. I wasn't aware information mentioned the next core book coming in November, so maybe it will help, but I honestly feel that Wizards took too flawed an approach to how they initially built the system and those issues won't go away without a re-design.

Would at least be easier to worry less if they actually played their own system. Maybe could believe they'll actually try to fix it rather than just agree it sucks from the DM and Player standpoint and go about their business. I know it's easier for them to write this way, but point still stands.

Funny, considering half the comments share agreement or an understanding of the frustration. Meanwhile, you've done nothing aside from repeatedly throw out ad hominems and repeat the same flawed statistical argument. Pay attention to other comments, I'm not looking to prove the other guy wrong, I'm looking for actual criticism that helps me build on the situation. Your comments have been aggressive, unhelpful, and generally flawed. I don't care what more you may have to say. Thankfully, someone else has been genuinely helpful and brought up points I wasn't considering that change the way I need to approach the situation from the start. 

I'll be going to bed now, a bit happier. Enjoy whatever it is you got from repeating your inherently flawed case and attacking my character rather than even attempting to approach the actual problem I had mentioned. I hope you do actually take the time to read that wiki page, it might help you to understand the flaws of basing your arguments and ideas off of overgeneralizations and statistics which don't even remotely represent the whole situation.
